title.en: Correcting name errors: acta aclaratoria, then re-record at the RPPC and Catastro
title.es: Corrección de errores de nombre: acta aclaratoria y nueva inscripción en RPPC y Catastro

what: A short notarial deed (acta aclaratoria) that clarifies and corrects an error in the original deed, such as a misspelled name, proven with the passport.
why: Banks, permit offices and future buyers will reject documents whose names don't match your passport. The correction must then be annotated at the RPPC and updated at Catastro, and the bank must update its own records.
who: The notario who issued the original deed, usually; then the RPPC, Catastro and the bank.
documents: The original deed, the passport (attached to the acta), and the payment for the RPPC annotation.
pitfalls: Fixing the RPPC but forgetting Catastro or the bank.
Applying for a bank power of attorney or permits before the bank's records match.
Send the registered acta aclaratoria to the bank separately; the bank's records are not updated automatically.

title.en: Annual trust fee
title.es: Anualidad del fideicomiso

what: The bank's yearly fee for acting as trustee, usually billed in advance each year on the anniversary of the trust.
why: It's part of the trust contract. Unpaid fees accrue penalties, and the bank can refuse to act (powers, permits, sale) until you're current.
who: The bank's trust-administration office.
documents: The fee notice and proof of payment. Always email the receipt to the bank.

cost.label: estimate
items: Late penalty 1.5% per the deed.
Some banks let you request the current amount online and then send a payment link or reference; ask your bank which channels it accepts this year.

pitfalls: Paying without sending the receipt, so the payment isn't applied to your trust.
Paying a peso amount at a branch at an unfavorable exchange rate when the contract is in USD (see step 3.7).
Learning about back fees only at sale. Get the yearly letter.

phrases.en: Please confirm the annual fee has been received and the trust is current.
phrases.es: Por favor confirme que se recibió la anualidad y que el fideicomiso está al corriente.

phrases.en: I'd like to file a complaint with your UNE.

sections.heading: Know your contract (fee disputes)
sections.markdown:
1. **Find the fee clause** in your trust deed: the amount, the **currency** (USD or MXN), how it **escalates** (fixed, by inflation, or "per the bank's current schedule"), the due date and the late penalty.
  2. **Pay the contract amount** in the contract currency. If the bank quotes pesos for a USD fee, ask which exchange rate it uses and on what date.
  3. If two offices quote different amounts, ask for the amount **in writing** from the trust office that administers your trust.
  4. **Keep every receipt**, and email each one to the trust office.
  5. Each year, ask for a **no-arrears letter** (*carta de no adeudo*). It's your proof if back fees are claimed when you sell or build.
  6. **Escalate in writing:** first to the bank's **UNE** (*Unidad Especializada de Atención a Usuarios*), which must answer **within 30 business days**; then to **CONDUSEF**, which can mediate (conciliation) and arbitrate. Filing with the UNE suspends the statute of limitations on your claim.

es.title: Anualidad del fideicomiso
es.what: La cuota anual del banco por actuar como fideicomiso, generalmente facturado por adelantado cada año en el aniversario del fideicomiso.
es.why: Es parte del contrato fideicomiso. Los cargos no pagados acumulan multas, y el banco puede negarse a actuar (poderes, permisos, venta) hasta que usted está en corriente.
es.who: La oficina de fideicomiso-administración del banco.
documents: El aviso de tarifas y la prueba de pago. Siempre envía el recibo al banco.
pitfalls: Pagar sin enviar el recibo, así que el pago no se aplica a su fideicomiso.
Pagar una cantidad de peso a una rama a un tipo de cambio desfavorable cuando el contrato está en USD (ver paso 3.7).
Aprendizaje sobre los gastos de espalda sólo a la venta. Consigue la carta anual.

sections.heading: Conozca su contrato (diferencias de pago)
sections.markdown:
1. **Encuentra la cláusula de tarifas**en tu escritura fideicomiso: la cantidad, el **currencia**(USD o MXN), cómo **escalaca**(fijo, por inflación, o "por el calendario actual del banco"), la fecha de vencimiento y la pena tardía.
  2. **Pagar el importe del contrato**en la moneda del contrato. Si el banco cotiza pesos por una cuota de USD, pregunte qué tipo de cambio utiliza y en qué fecha.
  3. Si dos oficinas citan diferentes cantidades, pida la cantidad **por escrito**de la oficina fideicomiso que administra su fideicomiso.
  4. **Mantenga cada recibo**, y envíe un correo electrónico a la oficina fideicomiso.
  5. Cada año, pida una carta **no-arrears**(*carta de no adeudo*). Es su prueba si se cobran los gastos de espalda cuando se vende o construye.
  6. **Escalate in writing:**first to the bank's **UNE**(*Unidad Especializada de Atención a Usuarios*), which must answer **within 30 business days**; then to **CONDUSEF**, which can mediate (conciliation) and arbitrate. La presentación de la UNE suspende el plazo de prescripción de su reclamación.

title.en: Banking and wires
title.es: Bancos y transferencias

what: Opening a Mexican bank account and moving money between countries.
why: Utilities, contractors and some taxes are easier to pay from a Mexican account; large transfers need a paper trail for your cost basis.
who: A Mexican bank; your home bank; or a regulated transfer service.
documents: Your passport and, for a full account, your INM resident card; proof of address; often your RFC (step 6.5). The CNBV's rules require an official ID such as a passport or INM document. Some banks offer non-resident accounts (for example, Scotiabank Mexico has advertised them); temporary and permanent residents can open regular accounts.

cost.label: estimate
cost.summary: Bank fees and FX spreads vary: compare quotes. Wires in MXN arrive via SPEI the same day inside Mexico.
cost.markdown: Bank fees and FX spreads vary: **compare quotes**. Wires in MXN arrive via SPEI the same day inside Mexico.

pitfalls: Wiring from an account not in the buyer's name (KYC problems); losing wire confirmations you need later to prove cost basis.

phrases.en: Can a non-resident open an account, and what documents do you need?
phrases.es: ¿Puede un no residente abrir una cuenta y qué documentos necesitan?

sections.heading: Home-country reporting
sections.markdown:
- **US:** report foreign accounts on **FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR)** if the combined balance exceeds **US$10,000** at any time in the year. A standard Mexican land trust is **not** a "foreign trust" for US tax purposes under **Rev. Rul. 2013-14**, so Forms 3520/3520-A are generally not required for it.
  - **Canada:** Form **T1135** applies to specified foreign property above **C$100,000** in total cost; a Mexican property used **primarily for personal use** is excluded, but a mainly rental property is reportable. Rental income still goes on your return (Form T776).

sections.heading: Exchange-rate tactics
sections.markdown: compare the all-in rate (spread plus fees) of your home bank, a regulated transfer service and a Mexican account; avoid converting USD fees at a branch counter; for large wires, ask for the rate in writing before sending; and pay USD-denominated fees (like many trust fees) in USD where the contract allows.

confirmWith: Confirm the details for your case with your notario or attorney.

es.title: Bancos y transferencias
es.what: Abrir una cuenta bancaria mexicana y mover dinero entre países.
es.why: Las utilidades, contratistas y algunos impuestos son más fáciles de pagar de una cuenta mexicana; las transferencias grandes necesitan un rastro de papel para su base de costo.
es.who: Un banco mexicano; su banco de origen; o un servicio de transferencia regulado.
documents: Su pasaporte y, para una cuenta completa, su tarjeta residente del INM; prueba de dirección; a menudo su RFC (paso 6.5). Las reglas del CNBV requieren una identificación oficial como un pasaporte o documento INM. Algunos bancos ofrecen cuentas no residentes (por ejemplo, Scotiabank México los ha anunciado); los residentes temporales y permanentes pueden abrir cuentas regulares.
pitfalls: Cableado de una cuenta no en el nombre del comprador (problemas de KYC); pérdida de confirmaciones de alambre que necesita más tarde para probar la base de costo.

sections.heading: Informe del país de origen
sections.markdown:
- **US:**reportar cuentas extranjeras en **FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR)**si el saldo combinado excede **US$10.000**en cualquier momento del año. Un fideicomiso de tierra mexicano estándar es **no**un "fideicomiso extranjero" con fines fiscales estadounidenses bajo **Rev. Rul. 2013-14**, por lo que los formularios 3520/3520-A generalmente no son necesarios para ello.
  - **Canadá:**Formulario **T1135**se aplica a la propiedad extranjera especificada más arriba **C$100,000**en costo total; se excluye una propiedad mexicana utilizada **principalmente para uso personal**, pero una propiedad principalmente de alquiler es reportable. Los ingresos de alquiler siguen su regreso (formulario T776).

sections.heading: Tácticas de tipo de cambio
sections.markdown: Compare la tarifa total (pread plus fees) de su banco de origen, un servicio de transferencia regulado y una cuenta mexicana; evite convertir las tasas de USD en un contador de rama; para los alambres grandes, pida la tarifa por escrito antes de enviar; y pagar las tasas de nominado USD (como muchos honorarios fideicomiso) en USD donde el contrato permite.

title.en: Transfer the utilities
title.es: Cambio de titular de los servicios

what: Putting electricity, water, gas, trash and internet accounts in your name (or confirming the account holder) after closing.
why: Unpaid utilities can be cut off, and the account holder receives the notices. Paid-up utility receipts are also proof of address for residency, banking and permits.
who: You, or your property manager with a power or letter.

cost.label: estimate
cost.summary: No published fee for CFE holder changes beyond any deposit; utility deposits and fees: confirm locally.
cost.markdown: No published fee for CFE holder changes beyond any deposit; utility deposits and fees: confirm locally.

pitfalls: Leaving the CFE account in the seller's name for years; summer bills jumping to the DAC tariff (step 4.8).

phrases.en: I'd like to change the account holder.
phrases.es: Quisiera hacer el cambio de titular.

sections.heading: Documents and steps
sections.markdown:
- **CFE (electricity):** change of account holder (*cambio de titular*) is done **in person** at a CFE service center (or by appointment through 071), not online. Bring ID, your RFC if you have one, the service number, a recent meter reading, and proof of ownership (deed or predial). The account must have no debts.
  - **Water (OOMSAPAS La Paz or Los Cabos):** change of account holder at the utility's office with the deed and ID; ask for a no-debt letter. Lots on trucked water (*pipa*) have no account.
  - **Propane (*gas LP*):** a tank refill service or a stationary tank contract; no government account.
  - **Trash:** municipal service or a private collector, depending on the area.
  - **Internet:** see step 4.16.

es.title: Cambio de titular de los servicios
es.what: Poner electricidad, agua, gas, basura y cuentas de Internet en su nombre (o confirmar el titular de la cuenta) después de cerrar.
es.why: Las utilidades no remuneradas pueden ser cortadas, y el titular de la cuenta recibe los avisos. Los recibos de utilidad de pago también son prueba de dirección para residencia, banca y permisos.
es.who: Usted, o su administrador de propiedades con un poder o una carta.
pitfalls: Dejando la cuenta CFE en nombre del vendedor durante años; las facturas de verano saltan al arancel DAC (paso 4.8).

sections.heading: Documentos y medidas
sections.markdown:
- **CFE (electricidad):**cambio de titular de cuenta (*cambio de titular*) se hace **en persona**en un centro de servicio CFE (o por cita previa a 071), no en línea. Traiga ID, su RFC si tiene uno, el número de servicio, una lectura reciente de medidores y prueba de propiedad (escritura o predial). La cuenta no debe tener deudas.
  - **Agua (OOMSAPAS La Paz o Los Cabos):**cambio de titular de cuenta en la oficina de la utilidad con la escritura e identificación; pida una carta de no-deuda. Muchas cantidades en agua camilla (*pipa*) no tienen cuenta.
  - **Propane (*gas LP*):**un servicio de recarga de tanques o un contrato de tanques fijos; ninguna cuenta gubernamental.
  - **Trash:**Servicio municipal o coleccionista privado, dependiendo de la zona.
  - **Internet:**ver el paso 4.16.

title.en: Bank power of attorney for permits (permits in the fiduciaria's name)
title.es: Poder de la fiduciaria para permisos (permisos a nombre de la fiduciaria)

what: The bank, not you, holds title, so licenses and permits are issued in the fiduciaria's name. The bank either signs each application or grants a power of attorney (poder) to you or your permit runner (gestor).
why: The trust's construction clause typically says that permits, licenses and appraisals are obtained in the trustee's name, and that completion is reported in its name.
who: The bank's trust office and its control desk (mesa de control), plus a notario to formalize the power.
documents: An instruction letter (carta de instrucción) on the bank's template, hand-signed (original mailed to the bank), adapted to your trust and the acts requested;
copies of passports;
the name of the attorney-in-fact (the person receiving the power);
the notario you choose;
your fees must be current and your names must match the bank's records.

cost.label: estimate
items: About USD 1,080 in total: about USD 500 for the notario to draft the power plus about USD 580 bank fee (confirmed Oct 2026).
No law-firm fee if you send the instruction letter to the bank yourself.
cost.markdown:
- About USD 1,080 in total: about USD 500 for the notario to draft the power plus about USD 580 bank fee (confirmed Oct 2026).
- No law-firm fee if you send the instruction letter to the bank yourself.

pitfalls: Some banks require permits to be issued in the fiduciaria's name; you sign as the bank's representative.
Filing permits in your own name (they'll be rejected or invalid).
Paying for several narrow powers.
Not including utilities (CFE, water), environmental filings and the completion notice in the power's scope.

1. Send the bank's trust desk an instruction letter with your original wet signature.
2. The bank instructs a notario you choose to draft the power of attorney.
3. The bank signs it.
4. Ask for one broad power that covers every permit (land use, building, utilities, environmental, completion).

es.title: Poder de la fiduciaria para permisos (permisos a nombre de la fiduciaria)
es.what: El banco, no usted, tiene título, así que las licencias y permisos se emiten en nombre de la fiduciaria. El banco firma cada aplicación o otorga un poder notarial (poder) a usted o su gestor (gertor).

sections.heading: Owner's representative and remote supervision (box)
sections.markdown:
- Consider an **independent supervisor** (*supervisor de obra*) who works for you, not the builder, especially if you're abroad.
  - Agree a **reporting cadence**: weekly photos and video, a monthly cost report against the budget, and copies of the **bitácora** entries (step 4.11).
  - Release each payment only after the supervisor confirms the milestone, and hold back the **retention** (*fondo de garantía*) until final acceptance.
  - Visit at key milestones (foundation, structure, roof slab, before finishes).
  - Supervisor fees: no published figure; get quotes.

sections.heading: The construction contract (checklist)
sections.markdown:
- **Type:** a fixed-price contract (*contrato de obra a precio alzado*) or cost-plus (*por administración*, cost plus a % fee). Fixed price moves cost risk to the builder; cost-plus needs tight reporting.
  - **Scope** tied to the stamped plans and a line-item budget (*presupuesto por partidas*) with specifications for materials and finishes.
  - **Payment schedule tied to milestones** you can verify (foundation, structure, roof slab, etc.), never large advances. A common practice is a **retention** (*fondo de garantía*, e.g., 5–10% of each payment) released after final acceptance (market practice, not law).
  - **Schedule and penalties** for delay (*penas convencionales*).
  - **Change orders** in writing, with price and time impact, signed before the work.

  - **Warranty:** the BCS Civil Code makes the builder liable after acceptance for defects from poor construction, bad materials or soil problems (art. 2548), but sets **no specific warranty period**, so write one into the contract (e.g., 1 year for finishes, longer for structure).
  - **Invoices with CFDI** for every payment. You need them to deduct construction cost when you sell (step 5.4).
  - Disputes: jurisdiction and language; a Spanish version usually prevails.

sections.heading: Supervisión representativa y remota del propietario (box)
sections.markdown:
- Considere un supervisor **independiente**(*supervisor de obra*) que trabaja para usted, no el constructor, especialmente si usted está en el extranjero.
  - Acorde un **reporting cadence**: fotos semanales y video, un informe mensual sobre costos contra el presupuesto, y copias de las entradas **bitácora**(paso 4.11).
  - Libere cada pago sólo después de que el supervisor confirme el hito, y retenga la **retención**(*fondo de garantía*) hasta la aceptación final.
  - Visita en hitos clave (fundación, estructura, tejado, antes de terminar).
  - Derechos de supervisión: no figura publicada; obtener cotizaciones.

sections.heading: El contrato de construcción (lista de control)
sections.markdown:
- **Tipo:**un contrato de precio fijo (*contrato de obra a precio alzado*) o costo-plus (*por administración*, costo más un % de cuota). El precio fijo mueve el riesgo de costo para el constructor; costo-plus necesita información estricta.
  - **Escope**atado a los planes estampados y un presupuesto de partida (*presupuesto por partidas*) con especificaciones para materiales y acabados.
  - **Pago fijado a hitos**se puede verificar (fundación, estructura, tejado, etc.), nunca grandes avances. Una práctica común es un **retención**(*fondo de garantía*, por ejemplo, 5–10% de cada pago) liberado después de la aceptación final (práctica del mercado, no ley).
  - **Programa y sanciones**para demora (*penas convencionales*).
  - **Cambiar pedidos**por escrito, con impacto de precio y tiempo, firmado antes del trabajo.
  - **IMSS**registro (SIROC) y quien paga contribuciones (paso 4.10); **quien tiene la licencia**y el bitácora; **seguro**(riesgo del constructor, responsabilidad de terceros).
  - **Garantía:**el Código Civil de la BCS hace que el constructor sea responsable después de la aceptación de defectos de construcción deficiente, materiales malos o problemas de suelo (art. 2548), pero establece **ningún período de garantía específico**, así que escriba uno en el contrato (por ejemplo, 1 año para acabados, más largo para estructura).
  - **Facturas con CFDI**para cada pago. Necesitas que deduzcan el costo de construcción cuando vendes (paso 5.4).
  - Diferencias: jurisdicción e idioma; generalmente prevalece una versión española.

sections.heading: Off-grid water options (no network)
sections.markdown:
- **Cistern + trucked water** (*cisterna + pipa*): the most common setup in rural Pescadero and Todos Santos. Size the cistern for at least a few weeks of use.
  - **Rainwater** is scarce in BCS but can supplement during the summer storm season.
  - **Small reverse-osmosis or desalination units** for brackish wells; a well still needs its concession, and brine discharge may need a CONAGUA discharge permit.
  - **Wastewater:** a septic tank and drain field (or a small treatment unit) designed from the percolation test; discharges to the ground fall under CONAGUA rules (NOM-006-CONAGUA for septic tanks).
  - Costs for these systems: **no published figure; get quotes**.

sections.markdown: most of BCS's hot localities are on subsidized residential tariffs (e.g., **1F**, for places with a summer average minimum of 33 °C), with a summer subsidy roughly May–October. That threshold is a key reason owners add solar.

title.en: IMSS for construction workers
title.es: IMSS para trabajadores de la construcción

what: Registering the construction project (obra) with IMSS (the Mexican social security institute) through SIROC and paying workers' social security.
why: If you hire workers directly, you are the employer in IMSS's eyes. The project must be registered in SIROC within 5 business days of starting. The usual approach is to hire a GC that registers its own workers and the obra.
who: The GC (preferred) or you.
documents: The building license, plans, and budget.

cost.label: estimate
items: IMSS presumes a minimum labor cost per m² for private construction and charges contributions on it if payroll reported is lower. For 2026 (from Feb 1, 2026), single-family homes: MXN 1,283/m² (social-interest), MXN 1,523/m² (medium), MXN 1,991/m² (residential/luxury).
At completion, IMSS can issue a statement that the labor reported was reasonable (carta de razonabilidad / no-debt), which some buyers and notaries ask for.
Registration needs an e.firma and an IMSS employer registration, which is why most owners have the GC register the project.
cost.markdown:
- IMSS presumes a **minimum labor cost per m²** for private construction and charges contributions on it if payroll reported is lower. For 2026 (from Feb 1, 2026), single-family homes: **MXN 1,283/m²** (social-interest), **MXN 1,523/m²** (medium), **MXN 1,991/m²** (residential/luxury). Contributions are a percentage of that labor cost; the exact rate depends on the risk class and salaries (**no single published rate**).

pitfalls: Paying cash to crews with no IMSS coverage. Liability after an accident falls on the owner.

title.en: Hurricane season and wind design
title.es: Temporada de huracanes y diseño contra viento

what: Designing for hurricane winds and storm water. BCS is hit regularly (the Eastern Pacific season runs May 15–Nov 30, with the highest risk roughly Aug–Oct).
why: The Reglamento de Construcciones de BCS requires structural design for wind; engineers use the CFE Manual de Diseño por Viento (2020), with site wind speeds from the INEEL "Sistema Viento" tool. Local press reports that the state regulation is outdated, so ask your engineer to design to the current CFE manual.
who: Your structural engineer (co-responsible for structural safety) and DRO.
pitfalls: Building in an arroyo; work scheduled for September, when storms halt sites.

phrases.en: Was the structure designed with the CFE wind manual for this site?
phrases.es: ¿La estructura se diseñó con el Manual de Diseño por Viento de CFE para este sitio?

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.markdown: roof-to-wall ties and slab roofs, impact-rated windows or shutters, anchored solar and tanks, elevation above arroyo flood lines (never build in an *arroyo* bed), drainage, and setbacks from the beach dune.

title.en: Substitute beneficiaries and inheritance
title.es: Fideicomisarios sustitutos y herencia

what: Naming who takes your beneficial rights when you die (fideicomisarios sustitutos), directly in the trust.
why: It usually avoids Mexican probate for the property.
who: The bank, and a notario for amendments.
documents: To change substitutes: an amendment instruction.
At death: a death certificate (apostilled and translated), IDs of the substitutes, and the bank's forms.
Most changes need an RNIE update within 40 business days.

cost.label: estimate
items: Acquisition tax on family inheritance or donation: 1.5% in Los Cabos and La Paz (see step 2.8).

pitfalls: Not naming substitutes.
Naming minors without a guardian structure.
Wills that conflict with the trust.
Forgetting the RPPC fee doubles for inheritance transfers (step 2.12).

phrases.en: I'd like to update my substitute beneficiaries.
phrases.es: Quisiera actualizar a mis fideicomisarios sustitutos.

sections.heading: Co-buyers
sections.markdown: name substitutes for *each* co-buyer; see the co-buyer agreement box in step 2.11.

sections.heading: Inheriting as a substitute beneficiary (step by step)
sections.markdown:
1. Get the **death certificate**, apostilled (if issued abroad) and translated by a perito (step 2.10).
  2. Notify the **trustee bank** and ask for its list of requirements and fees.
  3. The bank recognizes the substitute(s) by instruction or notarial act; the rights pass under the trust without probate.
  4. Pay the **acquisition tax** for family transfers where it applies (1.5% in La Paz and Los Cabos; step 2.8) and any recording fees (double for inheritance transfers at the RPPC, step 2.12).
  5. **Update the RNIE** (step 3.1) and name your own substitutes.
  6. Decide whether to **keep the trust** (and its remaining term) or sell (step 5.4).
  - Bank and notary fees: no published figure; ask your bank.

confirmWith: Confirm the details for your case with your notario or attorney.

es.title: Fideicomisarios sustitutos y herencia
es.what: Naming que toma tus derechos beneficiosos cuando mueres (fideicomisarios sustitutos), directamente en el fideicomiso.
es.why: Generalmente evita el probate mexicano para la propiedad.
es.who: El banco, y un notario para enmiendas.
documents: Cambiar sustitutos: una instrucción de enmienda.
A la muerte: un certificado de defunción (aprobado y traducido), identificaciones de los sustitutos y las formas del banco.
La mayoría de los cambios necesitan una actualización RNIE dentro de 40 días hábiles.
pitfalls: No nombrar sustitutos.
Nombrar a menores sin estructura tutelar.
Eso conflicto con el fideicomiso.
Olvidar los dobles de tarifas RPPC para transferencias de herencia (paso 2.12).

sections.heading: Co-buyers
sections.markdown: nombre sustituye a *each* co-buyer; vea el cuadro de acuerdo de co-buyer en el paso 2.11.

sections.heading: La herencia como un fideicomisario sustituto (paso a paso)
sections.markdown:
1. Obtenga el certificado **de la muerte**, destilado (si se emite en el extranjero) y traducido por un perito (paso 2.10).
  2. Notificar la **fiduciaria**y pedir su lista de requisitos y tarifas.
  3. El banco reconoce el sustituto o el acto notarial; los derechos pasan bajo el fideicomiso sin probate.
  4. Pagar el impuesto **de adquisición**para transferencias familiares donde se aplica (1,5% en La Paz y Los Cabos; paso 2.8) y cualquier tasa de registro (doble para transferencias de herencia en el RPPC, paso 2.12).
  5. **Actualizar el RNIE**(paso 3.1) y nombrar sus propios sustitutos.
  6. Decidir si mantener el fideicomiso**(y su término restante) o vender (paso 5.4).
  - Gastos bancarios y notarios: no figura publicada; pregunte a su banco.

title.en: Renting and taxes
title.es: Rentas e impuestos

what: Paying Mexican federal, state and municipal taxes on rental income.
why: Mexican-source income is taxable in Mexico, and lodging is also taxed locally.
who: You or a Mexican accountant (contador); platforms and trustees withhold part of it.
documents: RFC, CFDI invoices, platform withholding statements (constancias de retención), and the state lodging-tax registration.
pitfalls: Assuming the platform's withholding covers everything (it doesn't cover the state 4% or the municipal charge unless the platform says so).
Renting a condo where the bylaws ban short-term rentals.
Forgetting to report the income at home too (foreign tax credits may apply; get home-country advice).

phrases.en: Does the platform withhold income tax and VAT?
phrases.es: ¿La plataforma retiene ISR e IVA?

sections.heading: Federal income tax (ISR)
sections.markdown:
- **Non-resident landlord:** **25% of gross rent, no deductions** (LISR art. 158). The Mexican payer withholds it; if the payer is abroad, **you** file and pay within **15 days** of receiving the rent. When rent flows through the trust, the trustee can issue the invoice and withhold.
  - **Mexican tax resident using platforms:** platforms withhold **4% of lodging income** (LISR art. 113-A), or **20%** if you don't give them your RFC (art. 113-C).

sections.heading: VAT (IVA)
sections.markdown:
- **Short-term lodging and furnished rentals:** **16% IVA**. Platforms such as Airbnb collect IVA from guests and withhold **50%** of it if you've given your RFC, **100%** if not (LIVA art. 18-J).
  - **Long-term rental of an unfurnished home:** **exempt** from IVA (LIVA art. 20).

sections.heading: State lodging tax (BCS)
sections.markdown: **4%** of the lodging charge (*Impuesto sobre la Prestación de Servicios de Hospedaje*); register with the state and pay **monthly by the 15th**. One private tax site lists 5%; the official state procedure and 2026 tables show 4%.

sections.heading: La Paz environmental sanitation charge (from 2026)
Long-term lease basics
sections.markdown:
- Use a **written contract** in Spanish (with a translation), stating rent, term, deposit, who pays utilities, and the inventory if furnished.
  - The BCS Civil Code caps a residential lease at **10 years** (art. 2303).
  - Ask for a **deposit** (commonly one or two months, market practice) and a guarantee: a **fiador** (guarantor, ideally with property in BCS), a surety bond (*fianza*) or a rental-guarantee policy (*póliza jurídica*).
  - Unfurnished residential rent is **IVA-exempt**; furnished is not (see above). Rent paid by a Mexican company to a non-resident is subject to 25% withholding.

es.title: Rentas e impuestos
es.what: Pagar impuestos federales, estatales y municipales mexicanos sobre los ingresos de alquiler.
es.why: Los ingresos de origen mexicano son imponibles en México, y el alojamiento también se grava localmente.
es.who: Usted o un contable mexicano (contador); plataformas y fideicomisarios retienen parte de ella.
documents: RFC, facturas CFDI, declaraciones de retención de plataformas (constancias de retención), y el registro de alojamiento-tax estatal.
pitfalls: Suponiendo que la retención de la plataforma cubre todo (no cubre el estado 4% o la carga municipal a menos que la plataforma lo diga).
Alquilar un apartamento donde los estatutos prohíben alquileres a corto plazo.
Olvídate de reportar los ingresos en casa también (los créditos impositivos extranjeros pueden aplicarse; obtener asesoramiento en el país de origen).

sections.heading: Impuestos federales sobre la renta (ISR)
sections.markdown:
- **No-residente residente:****25% de alquiler bruto, sin deducciones**(art. 158 de la LISR). El pagador mexicano lo retiene; si el pagador está en el extranjero, **Usted**archiva y paga dentro de **15 días**de recibir el alquiler. Cuando el alquiler fluye a través del fideicomiso, el fideicomiso puede emitir la factura y retener.
  - **Residente fiscal mexicano usando plataformas:**plataformas retienen **4% de los ingresos de alojamiento**(art. 113-A), o **20%**si no les da su RFC (art. 113-C).

sections.heading: IVA (IVA)
sections.markdown:
- **Alojamiento corto plazo y alquileres amueblados: **16% IVA**. Plataformas como Airbnb recogen IVA de los huéspedes y retienen **50%**de él si usted ha dado su RFC, **100%**si no (Artículo LIVA 18-J).
  - **Alquiler a largo plazo de una casa sin muebles:****exento**del IVA (art. 20 de LIVA).

sections.heading: Impuesto estatal de alojamiento (BCS)
sections.markdown: **4%**del cargo de alojamiento (*Impuesto sobre la prestación de servicios de Hospedaje*); regístrese con el estado y pague **mensualmente por el día 15**. Un sitio de impuestos privado lista 5%; el procedimiento oficial del estado y 2026 tablas muestran 4%.

sections.heading: Saneamiento ambiental de La Paz (de 2026)
básicos de arrendamiento a largo plazo
sections.markdown:
- Utilice un contrato **escrito**en español (con una traducción), indicando alquiler, plazo, depósito, que paga utilidades, y el inventario si está amueblado.
  - El Código Civil de la BCS establece un contrato de arrendamiento residencial en **10 años**(art. 2303).
  - Solicitar un **deposit**(commonly one or two months, market practice) y una garantía: a **fiador**(guarantor, ideally with property in BCS), a surety bond (*fianza*) or a rental-guarantee policy (*póliza jurídica*).
  - Alquiler residencial no amueblado es **IVA-exento**; no amueblado (ver arriba). El alquiler pagado por una empresa mexicana a un no residente está sujeto a retención del 25%.

title.en: Selling
title.es: Venta

what: Either transferring your beneficial rights in the trust to the buyer (cesión de derechos fideicomisarios), or having the bank convey the property to the buyer or a new trust. Both are done before a notario.
why: It's the legal transfer. The notario withholds capital-gains tax.
who: A notario, the bank, and the buyer's attorney.
documents: The deed, the no-debt and no-lien certificates, proof of your cost basis (purchase deed, construction invoices with CFDI), and your RFC/CURP.

cost.label: estimate
items: Non-resident seller: 25% of the gross price with no deductions, or 35% of the net gain. When the sale is in a public deed, no Mexican legal representative is required to choose the 35% option; the notario calculates and withholds the tax (LISR art. 160).
How the gain is calculated (LISR arts. 119–124): 1. Start with the sale price.

Mexican tax-resident seller of their home: exempt up to 700,000 UDIS of sale price (≈MXN 6.2M at the Oct 2026 UDI value of ≈MXN 8.86), provided the sale is before a notary and you haven't used the exemption in the previous 3 years (LISR art. 93, fr. XIX). Above the cap, the excess is taxed proportionally.
If the trust ends, the bank must send the SRE an extinction notice within 40 business days.
cost.markdown:
- **Non-resident seller:** **25% of the gross price** with no deductions, **or** **35% of the net gain**. When the sale is in a public deed, **no Mexican legal representative is required** to choose the 35% option; the notario calculates and withholds the tax (LISR art. 160).
  - **How the gain is calculated (LISR arts. 119–124):**
    1. Start with the **sale price**.
    2. Subtract the **cost**, split into land and construction. **Land** keeps its full cost; **construction** (and improvements) loses **3% a year** of depreciation, down to a floor of **20%** of its cost. If the purchase deed doesn't split land from construction, the law presumes **20% land / 80% construction** (or uses the appraisal).
    3. **Index** both for inflation with the INPC from the purchase month to the sale month.
    4. Subtract the **sale costs**: notary and appraisal fees, the ISAI you paid at purchase, agent commissions, and **invoiced (CFDI) improvements**.
    5. The adjusted cost can't be less than **10% of the sale price**.
    6. In practice, an owner who built with full CFDI invoices usually pays far less under the 35%-of-gain option than under 25% of the gross. Without invoices, the construction cost may not count.
  - **Mexican tax-resident seller of their home:** exempt up to **700,000 UDIS** of sale price (≈MXN 6.2M at the Oct 2026 UDI value of ≈MXN 8.86), provided the sale is before a notary and you **haven't used the exemption in the previous 3 years** (LISR art. 93, fr. XIX). Above the cap, the excess is taxed proportionally. UDI value: [Banxico](https://www.banxico.org.mx/). You must declare tax residency in the deed and prove it with a constancia de residencia fiscal or tax ID card (RMF rule 3.11.3).
  - If the trust ends, the bank must send the SRE an **extinction notice within 40 business days**.

pitfalls: Construction invoices without CFDI can't be deducted.
An under-declared purchase price inflates your gain.
Unregistered construction (step 4.13).
The low recorded price trap: if your purchase deed shows a price below what you paid, your cost basis is lower and the taxable gain at sale is bigger. Don't agree to under-declare.
Get your RFC at purchase, not at sale (step 6.5), and ask for CFDI invoices for everything you build, so the deductions are ready when you sell.

Obtenga su RFC a la compra, no a la venta (paso 6.5), y pida facturas CFDI para todo lo que usted construye, por lo que las deducciones están listas cuando usted vende.

what: A homeowner's policy (seguro de casa habitación) covering fire, hydrometeorological perils (hurricane, flood, storm surge), earthquake, theft and liability; plus builder's risk during construction.
why: Not legally required, but the trust and your lender (if any) may require it, and hurricane losses in BCS are frequent.
who: A Mexican insurer authorized by the CNSF, usually through a local broker.

cost.label: estimate

sections.heading: Condo insurance (walls-out vs. all-in)
sections.markdown:
- **Walls-out** master policies cover the structure and common areas only; **all-in** policies also cover original interiors. Most resort condo master policies are walls-out, so you insure your **interior, contents, liability** and **loss assessment** yourself.
  - **Loss-assessment coverage** pays your share of a **special assessment** after a covered loss, including a master-policy deductible passed on to owners. It generally doesn't cover routine capital work or excluded perils.
  - Ask the administrator for the master policy's **declarations page** (*carátula*): perils, hurricane limits and deductible, flood treatment, and expiry.
  - After Hurricane Odile (2014), reported special assessments in some Los Cabos complexes ran to **five figures per unit** (around US$5,000–25,000+, reported). Your building may differ.
  - Insurer complaints go to [CONDUSEF](https://www.gob.mx/condusef).

es.title: Seguro de casa (huracanes y sismos)

es.why: No se requiere legalmente, pero el fideicomiso y su prestamista (si existe) pueden requerirlo, y las pérdidas de huracanes en BCS son frecuentes.

pitfalls: Suponiendo que la cubierta de huracanes esté incluida; confirme la cobertura "fenómenos hidrometeorológicos" y su deducible y la garantía.
Asegurar el valor del mercado en lugar de reconstruir el costo.
Políticas maestras de condominio que no cubren su interior.

sections.heading: Seguro de condominio (walls-out vs. all-in)
sections.markdown:
- **Las políticas magistrales abarcan solamente la estructura y las áreas comunes; **todo en**las políticas también cubren los interiores originales. La mayoría de las pólizas de condominio del complejo son murales, por lo que usted asegura su **interior, contenidos, responsabilidad**y **pérdida evaluación**usted mismo.

  - Pregunte al administrador por la página **declaraciones de la política maestra**(*carátula*): peligros, límites de huracanes y deducibles, tratamiento de inundaciones y caducidad.
  - Después del huracán Odile (2014), reportó evaluaciones especiales en algunos complejos de Los Cabos corrió a **cinco cifras por unidad**(alrededor de 5.000 a 25.000 dólares+, informó). Su edificio puede diferir.

title.es: Cuando su fiduciaria cambia o usted quiere cambiarla

what: What happens to your trust when the bank merges or sells its trust business, and how to move your trust to another bank voluntarily (sustitución de fiduciario).
why: Your trust contract, rights and term continue; but where you pay, who signs, and whose fee schedule applies can change.

cost.label: estimate
cost.summary: No published figures for release or acceptance fees; get both in writing
cost.markdown: No published figures for release or acceptance fees; get both in writing

pitfalls: Paying the old bank after a transfer; switching to save on the annual fee without counting the one-time switching costs.

phrases.en: Who is the trustee of my trust now?
phrases.es: ¿Quién es ahora el fiduciario de mi fideicomiso?

phrases.en: What would it cost to substitute the trustee?
phrases.es: ¿Cuánto costaría la sustitución de fiduciario?

sources.title: SRE – trustee substitutions in the annual report

sections.markdown: - **Example: CIBanco → Multiva (2025).** With the financial authorities' approval, CIBanco's trust business was transferred to **Banco Multiva**, effective **Sept 2, 2025**. Multiva became the successor trustee and took on all of CIBanco's rights and obligations as trustee, so the trusts continued. CIBanco's banking license was revoked on **Oct 10, 2025**.

sections.heading: If your bank changed (merger or transfer)
sections.markdown:
1. **Confirm in writing who your trustee is now** and ask for the new trust number, if any.
  2. Ask for the new **payment instructions** and your current fee and arrears status; don't pay into old accounts.
  3. Ask whether your **fee schedule** and currency stay the same (it's set by your contract; see step 3.5).
  4. Update your records, your property manager and your heirs.
  5. A merger usually needs nothing from you at the RNIE or RPPC, but ask the new trustee to confirm.

sections.heading: If you want to switch banks voluntarily
sections.markdown:
- Check your trust deed's clause on **removing or substituting the trustee**.
  - The new bank accepts the trust and both banks sign a **notarial deed of substitution**, recorded at the RPPC; the trustee reports it to the SRE in its annual report. Ask your attorney whether any SRE permit or RNIE update is needed in your case.
  - You pay the **old bank's release fee**, the **new bank's acceptance fee**, notary and RPPC fees.

es.title: Cuando su fiduciaria cambia o usted quiere cambiarla
es.what: Lo que le pasa a su fideicomiso cuando el banco fusiona o vende su negocio fideicomiso, y cómo mover su fideicomiso a otro banco voluntariamente (sustitución de crédito).
es.why: Su contrato fideicomiso, derechos y plazo continúan; pero donde usted paga, quién firma, y cuyo horario de tarifas se aplica puede cambiar.
pitfalls: Pagar el banco antiguo después de una transferencia; cambiar para ahorrar en la cuota anual sin contar los costos de conmutación de una sola vez.

sections.markdown: - **Ejemplo: CIBanco → Multiva (2025).**Con la aprobación de las autoridades financieras, el negocio fideicomiso de CIBanco fue transferido a **Banco Multiva**, eficaz **Sept 2, 2025**. Multiva se convirtió en el fideicomiso sucesor y asumió todos los derechos y obligaciones de CIBanco como fideicomisos, por lo que los fideicomisos continuaron. La licencia bancaria de CIBanco fue revocada en **Oct 10, 2025**.

sections.heading: Si su banco cambió (merger o transferencia)
sections.markdown:
1. **Confirma por escrito quién es tu fideicomiso ahora**y pide el nuevo número fideicomiso, si lo hay.
  2. Pida las nuevas instrucciones de pago ****y su tarifa actual y su estado de atraso; no pague en cuentas viejas.
  3. Pregúntese si su horario **sentido**y la moneda permanecen igual (se establece por su contrato; vea el paso 3.5).
  4. Actualice sus registros, su administrador de propiedades y sus herederos.
  5. Una fusión generalmente no necesita nada de usted en el RNIE o RPPC, pero pide al nuevo fiduciario que confirme.

sections.heading: Si quieres cambiar los bancos voluntariamente
sections.markdown:
- Revisa la cláusula de tu fideicomiso escritura sobre **removiendo o sustituyendo al fideicomiso**.
  - El nuevo banco acepta el fideicomiso y ambos bancos firman una escritura notarial de sustitución**, registrada en el RPPC; el fideicomiso lo reporta al SRE en su informe anual. Pregúntele a su abogado si cualquier permiso SRE o actualización RNIE es necesaria en su caso.
  - Usted paga la cuota de liberación del banco **, la tarifa de aceptación del banco **, notario y tasas de RPPC.

title.en: Owning from abroad: managers, caretakers, squatters and hurricane prep
title.es: Ser propietario a distancia: administradores, cuidadores, invasores y preparación para huracanes

what: Keeping the property safe, paid up and maintained while you're away.
why: Most owners are away for part of the year. Vacant lots attract squatters (see the usucapión periods in step 1.14), and hurricane season overlaps the months many owners leave.
who: A property manager (rental and full-service), a caretaker (cuidador, owner-away checks), and you.

cost.label: estimate
items: Reported market ranges in Los Cabos and Todos Santos (2026): short-term rental management ~15–30% of gross rental revenue (full-service often ~25%); long-term rental management ~8–12% of monthly rent; owner-away caretaker service ~MXN 6,000–10,000 per month, with extra visits billed separately.
cost.markdown: - Reported market ranges in Los Cabos and Todos Santos (2026): short-term rental management **~15–30% of gross rental revenue** (full-service often ~25%); long-term rental management **~8–12% of monthly rent**; owner-away caretaker service **~MXN 6,000–10,000 per month**, with extra visits billed separately.

pitfalls: No written scope; a manager collecting rent without reports; leaving in September without storm prep.

phrases.en: Please send monthly photos and receipts.
phrases.es: Por favor envíe fotos y recibos cada mes.

sections.heading: Checklist for a manager or caretaker
sections.markdown:
- A written contract: scope, fees, how they spend your money, monthly reporting with **photos and receipts**, and who holds keys and alarm codes.
  - A **limited power of attorney** or a signed letter for specific acts (paying utilities, receiving notices, dealing with repairs). Don't give a general power, and don't lend them your foreign-plated car (step 6.8).
  - If they employ staff at your home, see step 5.10.

sections.heading: Protecting a vacant lot (squatters)
sections.markdown: keep boundary markers and a fence or wall where allowed; post a sign; have someone visit regularly and photograph the lot; keep **predial current** and the receipts; and act fast with your attorney if anyone moves on.

sections.heading: Hurricane pre-departure checklist
sections.markdown: shutters or impact protection in place; drains, gutters and the cistern cleared; loose items, solar panels and tanks secured; propane closed; photos and video of the house and contents for insurance; policy numbers and the broker's contact shared with your manager; a post-storm inspection plan.

confirmWith: Confirm the details for your case with your notario or attorney.

es.title: Ser propietario a distancia: administradores, cuidadores, invasores y preparación para huracanes
es.what: Manteniendo la propiedad segura, pagada y mantenida mientras estás fuera.
es.why: La mayoría de los propietarios están fuera por parte del año. Los lotes vacantes atraen a los ocupantes (ver los períodos de usucapión en el paso 1.14), y la temporada de huracanes superpone los meses que muchos propietarios abandonan.
es.who: Un administrador de propiedades (rental y servicio completo), un cuidador (cuidador, cheques de salida del propietario), y usted.
pitfalls: No hay alcance escrito; un gerente que recoge alquiler sin reportes; saliendo en septiembre sin prepa de tormenta.

sections.heading: Lista de verificación para un administrador o cuidador
sections.markdown:
- Un contrato escrito: alcance, tarifas, cómo gastan su dinero, reportando mensualmente con **fotos y recibos**, y que tiene claves y códigos de alarma.
  - A **limited poder notarial**o una carta firmada para actos específicos (pagando utilidades, recibiendo avisos, tratando con reparaciones). No le des un poder general, y no les prestes tu coche con chapa extranjera (paso 6.8).
  - Si emplean personal en su casa, vea el paso 5.10.

sections.heading: Proteger un lote vacante (squatters)
sections.markdown: mantener los marcadores de límites y una cerca o pared donde se permite; publicar una señal; hacer que alguien visite regularmente y fotografiar el lote; mantener **corriente previa**y los recibos; y actuar rápido con su abogado si alguien se mueve.

sections.markdown: persianas o protección de impacto en su lugar; drenajes, canaletas y cisterna despejadas; elementos sueltos, paneles solares y tanques asegurados; propano cerrado; fotos y vídeo de la casa y contenidos para seguros; números de póliza y el contacto del corredor compartido con su gerente; un plan de inspección posterior a la tormenta.

title.en: If you employ people at your home (housekeeper, gardener, caretaker)
title.es: Si emplea personas en su casa (trabajadora del hogar, jardinero, cuidador)

what: Your duties as an employer (persona empleadora) of household workers under Mexican labor and social-security law.
why: Household workers have the rights in the Ley Federal del Trabajo (arts. 331–343), and since May 2023 employers must register them with IMSS from the first day of work.

cost.label: estimate
cost.summary: IMSS contributions depend on salary and days worked; IMSS's calculator gives the amount. No single published figure.
cost.markdown: IMSS contributions depend on salary and days worked; IMSS's calculator gives the amount. No single published figure.

pitfalls: Paying cash with no IMSS registration (you're liable for accidents and back contributions); forgetting the aguinaldo; dismissing without a signed finiquito.

phrases.en: Is the service company the employer?
phrases.es: ¿La empresa de servicios es el patrón?

phrases.en: I'd like to register my household worker with IMSS.
phrases.es: Quisiera inscribir a mi persona trabajadora del hogar en el IMSS.

sections.markdown: - **Employee or service company?** If you hire a person directly and set their schedule, you're the employer. If a company sends the worker and invoices you, the company is the employer; ask for proof of its IMSS registration.

sections.heading: Key obligations
sections.markdown:
- **IMSS registration:** online or at the IMSS office, with your **CURP** and the worker's data (social security number, CURP, salary, days worked). Registration is free; IMSS calculates the contributions, the first month is paid in arrears and later months in advance, and INFONAVIT housing contributions are included.
  - **Minimum wage 2026:** **MXN 315.04 per day** in BCS (general zone).
  - **Aguinaldo:** at least **15 days' pay**, paid **before December 20** (prorated for part of a year) (LFT art. 87).
  - **Vacation:** after one year, at least **12 days**, rising with seniority, plus a **vacation premium of at least 25%** (LFT arts. 76, 80).
  - **Rest days and hours** for live-in and live-out workers (LFT arts. 333, 336).
  - **Ending employment:** on resignation, the worker gets a **finiquito** (pay owed, prorated aguinaldo, vacation and premium). On dismissal without legal cause, a **liquidación** generally adds **3 months' pay**, and may add 20 days per year of service and a **seniority premium of 12 days per year** (LFT arts. 48–50, 162). Get a Mexican labor attorney or accountant to calculate it and to prepare a signed settlement.

es.title: Si emplea personas en su casa (trabajadora del hogar, jardinero, cuidador)
es.what: Sus deberes como empleador (persona empleadora) de los trabajadores domésticos bajo la legislación laboral y de seguridad social mexicana.
es.why: Los trabajadores domésticos tienen los derechos en la Ley Federal del Trabajo (arts. 331 a 343), y desde mayo de 2023 los empleadores deben registrarlos en el IMSS desde el primer día de trabajo.
pitfalls: Pagando en efectivo sin registro IMSS (se te hace responsable de accidentes y contribuciones de respaldo); olvidando el aguinaldo; descartando sin un finiquito firmado.

sections.markdown: - **Employee or service company?**Si contratas a una persona directamente y fijas su horario, eres el empleador. Si una empresa envía al trabajador y le factura, la empresa es el empleador; pida pruebas de su registro de IMSS.

sections.heading: Obligaciones clave
sections.markdown:
- **Inscripción del MSS:**en línea o en la oficina del IMSS, con su **CURP**y los datos del trabajador (número de seguridad social, CURP, sueldo, días trabajados). El registro es gratuito; el IMSS calcula las contribuciones, el primer mes se paga en atrasos y meses posteriores de antelación, y las contribuciones de vivienda INFONAVIT se incluyen.
  - **Salario mínimo 2026:****MXN 315.04 por día**en BCS (zona general).
  - **Aguinaldo:**al menos **15 días de pago**, pagados **antes del 20 de diciembre**(prorrateados por parte de un año) (LFT art. 87).
  - **Vacación:**después de un año, al menos **12 días**, subiendo con antigüedad, más una prima **vacación de al menos 25%**(LFT arts. 76, 80).
  - **Los mejores días y horas**para los trabajadores vivos y vivos (artículos 333, 336).
  - **Definir el empleo:**de la renuncia, el trabajador obtiene un **finiquito**(debido, prorrateado aguinaldo, vacaciones y prima). En caso de despido sin causa legal, una **liquidación**generalmente añade **3 meses de sueldo**, y puede añadir 20 días al año de servicio y una **prima de senioridad de 12 días al año**(artículos 48 a 50, 162). Obtenga un abogado o contador mexicano para calcularlo y preparar un acuerdo firmado.

title.en: Choose: visitor (FMM) vs. temporary vs. permanent residency
title.es: Elija: visitante (FMM), residencia temporal o permanente

what: Visitor (FMM / visitante): US and Canadian citizens enter visa-free for up to 180 days. The INM officer decides the number of days. No work for Mexican employers. Temporary resident: 1 to 4 years, renewable. Remote work for foreign employers is allowed. Permanent resident: indefinite. Obtained directly at a consulate (typically retirees with a pension), by family ties, or after 4 years as a temporary resident.
why: Staying longer than visitor status allows, or wanting local banking, a CURP and resident convenience, calls for residency.
who: You, the Mexican consulate in your home country, and then INM in Mexico.
documents: Passport. See step 6.3 for the rest.

cost.label: estimate
items: The FMM fee is built into air tickets (MXN 983 under LFD 2026).
The consular residency visa fee is about US$56 (Toronto shows CAD 80–82).
cost.markdown:
- The FMM fee is built into air tickets (**MXN 983** under LFD 2026).
  - The consular residency visa fee is about **US$56** (Toronto shows CAD 80–82).

pitfalls: Owning property does not give you residency.
A property held in a trust generally doesn't satisfy the real-estate route, which needs a deed in the applicant's own name worth over 91,710 UMA-days (≈ MXN 10.76 million in 2026).

title.en: Enter Mexico and do the canje at INM within 30 days
title.es: Entre a México y haga el canje en el INM dentro de 30 días

what: The consular visa is a single-entry sticker valid for 180 days. At entry, the officer must record you as entering to exchange the visa (canje), not as a tourist. Then, within 30 calendar days, you apply at INM to swap the visa for a resident card.
why: Ley de Migración and the INM procedures. If entry is recorded as tourist, the visa is lost.
who: INM. La Paz municipality: the INM office in La Paz. Los Cabos: the INM office in Cabo San Lucas.
documents: Passport, the FMM marked for canje, the online INM form, the payment receipt and photos. Fingerprints are taken at the office.

cost.label: estimate
items: Temporary card: MXN 11,141 (1 year), 16,693 (2 years), 21,143 (3 years).
Permanent card: MXN 13,579.
Resolution in up to 15 business days. Owners report anything from same-day card issue to several weeks at the La Paz and Cabo San Lucas offices (anecdotal, 2025–2026); plan for the longer end.

pitfalls: Faltan 30 días.

title.en: How residency affects buying and owning

sections.heading: What changes
sections.markdown:
- **Capital gains on sale:** the primary-residence exemption (up to 700,000 UDIS) generally requires **Mexican tax residency**, proved to the notario (step 5.4).
  - **Easier paperwork:** a CURP and RFC make CFE contracts, invoices and permits smoother.
  - **Rental taxes:** Mexican tax residents file under resident rules instead of the flat 25% non-resident withholding.

sections.heading: What doesn't change
sections.markdown:
- **The trust.** Residents still need a fideicomiso in the restricted zone. Only Mexican nationality changes that.
  - Your annual trust fee, RNIE obligations and predial.

sections.heading: Important
sections.markdown: A resident card is **not** the same as being a **tax** resident. Tax residency depends on where your home and center of vital interests are, and on the treaties with the US and Canada.

title.es: Salud y seguros para residentes

what: Your options for medical care as a resident: IMSS voluntary enrollment, private insurance, and evacuation coverage.
why: Visitor travel insurance usually stops once you live in Mexico, and Medicare doesn't pay for care in Mexico.
who: IMSS (subdelegation for your address), your insurer or broker.

cost.label: estimate

cost.markdown: Private premiums: no published figure; get quotes. Insurer complaints: [CONDUSEF](https://www.gob.mx/condusef).

phrases.en: What does voluntary IMSS enrollment require?
phrases.es: ¿Qué requisitos tiene la incorporación voluntaria al IMSS?

sections.heading: Options
sections.markdown:
- **IMSS voluntary health insurance for families** (*Seguro de Salud para la Familia*, "Modalidad 33"): for people not covered by another IMSS regime. Needs a **CURP**, an IMSS number, ID and proof of address; coverage starts the first day of the following month. **2026 annual cost per person by age** (reported): about **MXN 9,300** (0–19) up to **MXN 20,600** (60–69), **21,500** (70–79) and **22,150** (80+). Serious **pre-existing conditions are excluded** (for example cancer, kidney or heart failure, HIV, serious mental illness), and waiting periods apply to some treatments.
  - **Private major-medical insurance** (*gastos médicos mayores*) from Mexican or international insurers; premiums rise sharply with age and exclude pre-existing conditions for a period.
  - **Medical evacuation or air-ambulance membership** to the US or Canada.
  - **Where care is:** IMSS general hospitals and the state public hospitals in **La Paz** and in the **Los Cabos** area, plus private hospitals in La Paz, San José del Cabo and Cabo San Lucas. Rural areas (El Pescadero, Todos Santos, the East Cape) have clinics; serious cases go to La Paz or Los Cabos.

sections.heading: Opciones
sections.markdown:
- **Seguro médico voluntario para familias**(* Seguro de Salud para la Familia*, "Modalidad 33"): para personas no cubiertas por otro régimen del IMSS. Necesita un **CURP**, un número de IMSS, ID y prueba de dirección; la cobertura comienza el primer día del mes siguiente. **2026 costo anual por persona por edad**(reportado): aproximadamente **MXN 9,300**(0–19) hasta **MXN 20,600**(60–69), **21.500**(70–79) y **22.150**(80+). Se excluyen las condiciones graves **preexistentes**(por ejemplo, cáncer, insuficiencia renal o cardíaca, VIH, enfermedad mental grave), y los períodos de espera se aplican a algunos tratamientos.
  - **Seguro médico primario privado**(*gastos médicos mayores*) de aseguradores mexicanos o internacionales; primas aumentan marcadamente con la edad y excluyen las condiciones preexistentes durante un período.

  - **Dónde está la atención:**Hospitales generales del IMSS y hospitales públicos estatales en **La Paz**y en la zona **Los Cabos**, además de hospitales privados en La Paz, San José del Cabo y Cabo San Lucas. Zonas rurales (El Pescadero, Todos Santos, el Cabo Este) tienen clínicas; casos graves van a La Paz o Los Cabos.

title.en: Ejido deep check: dominio pleno, PROCEDE/FANAR and the RAN file
title.es: Revisión a fondo de ejido: dominio pleno, PROCEDE/FANAR y el expediente del RAN

what: Before you pay anything for land that was ever ejido, prove the whole chain: the parcel was measured and certified (PROCEDE or FANAR), the ejido assembly approved dominio pleno, the RAN cancelled the agrarian registration (baja), and the land now has a private title recorded at the state public registry (RPPC).
why: Ejido land is common in Baja California Sur, including on the coast. A parcel certificate or an 'assignment of rights' is not private ownership, and foreigners cannot hold ejido rights directly. Gaps in this chain are one of the most common ways buyers lose money.
who: Your independent attorney pulls the RAN file and the RPPC record; the notario confirms the title can be transferred. You can look up the ejido yourself in the RAN's public PHINA database.
documents: Parcel certificate (certificado parcelario) or plot title (título de solar), if any
Minutes of the ejido assembly approving dominio pleno, with attendance and quorum
RAN record showing the agrarian registration was cancelled (baja del RAN)
Private title and its RPPC recording (folio real)
Proof the right of first refusal (derecho del tanto) was respected on the first sale
Survey matching the RAN plan

cost.label: estimate
cost.summary: attorney review of an ejido file is usually a flat fee; RAN and registry copies are modest official fees. Conversion costs vary widely and are normally the seller's.
items: Attorney ejido due diligence: often around US$1,000–3,000 (estimate; get a written quote).
RAN and RPPC certified copies: official fees, usually a small share of the total (estimate; check the current fee schedule).
cost.markdown:
- Attorney ejido due diligence: often around US$1,000–3,000 (estimate; get a written quote).
- RAN and RPPC certified copies: official fees, usually a small share of the total (estimate; check the current fee schedule).

timing.note: Checking a finished file: about 2–6 weeks. A conversion to dominio pleno still in progress: often 6–18 months or more, and it can fail.

pitfalls: Paying a deposit on a 'cesión de derechos' or parcel certificate as if it were a title.
Assembly minutes without proper notice, quorum or a Procuraduría Agraria representative, which can be challenged later.
Skipping the derecho del tanto: family and ejido members can later claim the sale is void.
Common-use land (tierras de uso común) sold as if it were a parcel.
Boundaries in the RAN plan that don't match the ground.

phrases.en: Has the parcel already been removed from the RAN and recorded at the public registry?
phrases.es: ¿La parcela ya se dio de baja en el RAN y está inscrita en el Registro Público?

phrases.en: May I see the assembly minutes that approved dominio pleno?
phrases.es: ¿Me permite ver el acta de asamblea que aprobó el dominio pleno?

phrases.en: Was the right of first refusal respected?
phrases.es: ¿Se respetó el derecho del tanto?

sections.heading: Checklist, in order
sections.markdown:
1. Find the ejido in PHINA and confirm the parcel exists.
2. Get the parcel certificate and the RAN plan.
3. Get the dominio pleno assembly minutes; check notice, quorum and attendance.
4. Confirm the baja del RAN.
5. Confirm a private title recorded at the RPPC, plus a no-lien certificate.
6. Confirm the derecho del tanto was respected on the first sale.
7. Only then sign a promise to purchase.

es.title: Revisión a fondo de ejido: dominio pleno, PROCEDE/FANAR y el expediente del RAN
es.what: Antes de pagar cualquier cosa por un terreno que alguna vez fue ejidal, compruebe toda la cadena: la parcela se midió y certificó (PROCEDE o FANAR), la asamblea ejidal aprobó el dominio pleno, el RAN canceló la inscripción agraria (baja) y el terreno ya tiene un título privado inscrito en el Registro Público de la Propiedad (RPPC).
es.why: La tierra ejidal es común en Baja California Sur, incluso en la costa. Un certificado parcelario o una 'cesión de derechos' no es propiedad privada, y los extranjeros no pueden ser titulares de derechos ejidales directamente. Las fallas en esta cadena son una de las formas más comunes en que los compradores pierden dinero.
es.who: Su abogado independiente obtiene el expediente del RAN y el folio del RPPC; el notario confirma que el título se puede transmitir. Usted mismo puede consultar el ejido en la base pública PHINA del RAN.
documents: Certificado parcelario o título de solar, si existe
Acta de asamblea ejidal que aprueba el dominio pleno, con lista de asistencia y quórum
Constancia del RAN de la baja de la inscripción agraria
Título de propiedad privado y su inscripción en el RPPC (folio real)
Constancia de que se respetó el derecho del tanto en la primera venta
Levantamiento topográfico que coincida con el plano del RAN
pitfalls: Pagar un anticipo por una 'cesión de derechos' o un certificado parcelario como si fuera un título.
Actas de asamblea sin convocatoria correcta, quórum o representante de la Procuraduría Agraria, que pueden impugnarse después.
Omitir el derecho del tanto: familiares y ejidatarios pueden reclamar después la nulidad de la venta.
Tierras de uso común vendidas como si fueran una parcela.
Linderos del plano del RAN que no coinciden con el terreno.

timing.note: Revisar un expediente terminado: aprox. 2 a 6 semanas. Una conversión a dominio pleno en proceso: a menudo de 6 a 18 meses o más, y puede no lograrse.

sections.heading: Lista de verificación, en orden
sections.markdown:
1. Busque el ejido en PHINA y confirme que la parcela existe.
2. Obtenga el certificado parcelario y el plano del RAN.
3. Obtenga el acta de asamblea de dominio pleno; revise convocatoria, quórum y asistencia.
4. Confirme la baja del RAN.
5. Confirme un título privado inscrito en el RPPC, más un certificado de libertad de gravámenes.
6. Confirme que se respetó el derecho del tanto en la primera venta.
7. Solo entonces firme una promesa de compraventa.

es.confirmWith: Confirme los detalles de su caso con su notario o abogado.

cost.summary: la revisión de un expediente ejidal suele cobrarse como honorario fijo; las copias del RAN y del registro son derechos oficiales modestos. El costo de la conversión varía mucho y normalmente lo cubre el vendedor.
items: Revisión ejidal por abogado: a menudo alrededor de US$1,000 a 3,000 (estimación; pida cotización por escrito).
Copias certificadas del RAN y del RPPC: derechos oficiales, normalmente una parte pequeña del total (estimación; consulte la tarifa vigente).

title.en: Coastal due diligence: ZOFEMAT, setbacks, erosion and beach access
title.es: Revisión de propiedades costeras: ZOFEMAT, restricciones, erosión y acceso a la playa

what: For beachfront or near-beach property, confirm where the federal maritime zone (ZOFEMAT, generally the first 20 m inland from the high-tide line) begins, whether anyone holds a concession over it, which municipal and environmental setbacks apply, and whether the shore erodes or floods in storms.
why: Nobody can own the federal zone; you can only hold a concession to use it. Structures on it without a concession can be ordered removed, and the line can move after storms.
who: A surveyor maps the high-tide line and the federal zone; your attorney checks SEMARNAT concession records and the municipal land-use plan.
documents: Survey showing the ZOFEMAT line
Any existing ZOFEMAT concession title and proof its duties are paid
Municipal land-use and setback information
Environmental restrictions (protected areas, dunes, turtle nesting)

cost.label: estimate
cost.summary: coastal survey and attorney review are quoted per job; ZOFEMAT duties are annual federal fees per m² that vary by zone and use.
items: Coastal survey with ZOFEMAT line: often US$500–2,000 depending on size and access (estimate).
ZOFEMAT annual duties: per m², set in the federal duties law and updated yearly (estimate; confirm the current rate).
cost.markdown:
- Coastal survey with ZOFEMAT line: often US$500–2,000 depending on size and access (estimate).
- ZOFEMAT annual duties: per m², set in the federal duties law and updated yearly (estimate; confirm the current rate).

timing.note: Survey: about 1–3 weeks. Concession records check: weeks. A new concession or a transfer can take many months (estimate).

pitfalls: Assuming the seller's beach patio or palapa is part of the property.
Unpaid concession duties carried over to you.
Buying in an arroyo or low dune that floods in hurricanes.
Blocking public beach access, which the law protects.

phrases.en: Is there a ZOFEMAT concession in front of this lot, and who holds it?
phrases.es: ¿Hay una concesión de ZOFEMAT frente a este lote y quién es el titular?

phrases.en: Where exactly is the federal zone line?
phrases.es: ¿Dónde está exactamente la línea de la zona federal?

sources.title: Reglamento de Construcciones para el Estado de BCS
